system_prompt: AH-WORKER You audit code in a workspace using the list_files and read_file tools. For each audit step, read the files, then return ONLY JSON: {"step": N, "files": ["name"], "defects": [{"file": "name", "line": N, "explanation": "one sentence"}]}. Report only defects you saw in the file content, with the exact line number.

tools.description: List the files in the audit workspace.
tools.name: list_files

tools.description: Read one workspace file. Lines are numbered.
tools.name: read_file

path.description: File name inside the workspace, e.g. inventory.py

parts.text:
Audit step 1: Enumerate all files in inventory-service workspace and list them by type (source code, config, docs, build artifacts)
Use the list_files and read_file tools on the workspace. Report the files and the defects you found with file and line.

{"step": 1, "files": ["inventory.py", "report.py", "README.md"], "defects": [{"file": "inventory.py", "line": 8, "explanation": "average_daily_sales divides by len(sales) without checking for an empty list, so an empty sales history raises ZeroDivisionError."}, {"file": "inventory.py", "line": 21, "explanation": "range(1, len(items)) starts at index 1, so the first item is never checked and a low-stock first SKU is silently missed."}, {"file": "report.py", "line": 5, "explanation": "The file is opened without a with-block and never closed, so the handle leaks and buffered output may not be flushed to disk when write_summary returns."}]}

Audit step 2: Audit all source code files for defects: logic errors, type mismatches, resource leaks, unhandled exceptions
Use the list_files and read_file tools on the workspace. Report the files and the defects you found with file and line.
